evidence: Thin ﬁlms of ErFeO 3 are grown on top of 4 ″ SiO2 (100 nm)/Si substrates in a commercial ﬂow-type ALD reactor (F-120 by ASM Microchemistry Ltd.) under a pressure of 15–16 mbar, using metalorganic Er(thd)3 and Fe(thd)3 (thd = 2,2,6,6-tetramethylheptane-3,5-dionate) as metal precursors. Ozone is used as oxidizing agent, injected into the reactor at a concentration of about 200 g/nm3. N 2 is employed as carrier and purging gas. First, the ALD of the binary Er2O3 and Fe2O3 ﬁlms has been optimized, in order to identify the optimal growth conditions for the ternary alloys. Fe and Er precursors are evaporated at T = 110 °C and T = 150 °C respectively. The pulsing time applied for Er(thd)3 and Fe(thd)3 was 1 s each, as reported in Ref. and, while for O 3 and N2 purge pulses we chose longer times (4 s and 6 s respectively), long enough to guarantee saturation and to avoid CVD components.
